## How it works

- [statement] Playground execution displays results in a Playground Results pane, or in a new tab if split view is disabled. (medium confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/mongodb-vscode/run-agg-pipelines.md · keywords: MongoDB for VS Code playgrounds and mongosh scripts · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/mongodb-vscode/require-playgrounds/require-local.md

## How-to and procedures

- [statement] Use `require()` to reuse local JavaScript code or load native and external Node modules in playgrounds. MongoDB documents a local validation helper exported with `module.exports` and imported by file path. (medium confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/mongodb-vscode/require-playgrounds.md · keywords: MongoDB for VS Code playgrounds and mongosh scripts · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/mongodb-vscode/require-playgrounds/require-local.md
- [statement] Use the Command Palette command MongoDB: Create MongoDB Playground to open a playground with sample commands. (medium confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/mongodb-vscode/crud-ops.md · keywords: MongoDB for VS Code playgrounds and mongosh scripts · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/mongodb-vscode/run-agg-pipelines.md

## Problems, failure modes and limitations

- [statement] For command-line script execution, mongosh documents `--file` or `-f` and recommends always using these flags when passing filenames because bare filenames can fail with other arguments. (medium confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/mongodb-shell/write-scripts.md · keywords: MongoDB for VS Code playgrounds and mongosh scripts · also: https://github.com/mongodb-js/mongosh

## Comparisons and alternatives

- [statement] MongoDB Playgrounds provide a JavaScript environment in VS Code for prototyping queries, aggregations, CRUD operations, and MongoDB commands. Saved playgrounds can document database interactions alongside application code. (medium confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/mongodb-vscode/playgrounds.md · keywords: MongoDB for VS Code playgrounds and mongosh scripts · also: https://github.com/mongodb-js/vscode, https://www.mongodb.com/docs/mongodb-vscode/crud-ops.md
- [statement] Playground logging and query results use different destinations: console messages appear in the VS Code Output panel, while Playground Results appear in an editor pane or tab. An output troubleshooting thread reports confusion between these destinations. (medium confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/mongodb-vscode/playgrounds.md · keywords: MongoDB for VS Code playgrounds and mongosh scripts · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/mongodb-vscode/run-agg-pipelines.md, https://stackoverflow.com/questions/66408490/mongodb-playground-output-not-showing-in-vs-code-terminal
- [statement] A November 2021 issue report says extension v0.6.10 returned `[COMMON-90002] load is not currently implemented for this platform` even though the reporter could use load in Mongosh 1.1.0; a maintainer replied that the implementation had not yet been exposed in VS Code playgrounds. This is historical evidence, not a current compatibility guarantee. (low confidence) — https://github.com/mongodb-js/vscode/issues/263
- [statement] Playground messages from `console.log()`, `print()`, and `printjson()` appear in the VS Code Output panel. (low confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/mongodb-vscode/playgrounds.md

## Facts and statements

- [statement] The Play button runs the playground against the active deployment. Selecting lines enables execution of just that portion for focused testing and troubleshooting. (low confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/mongodb-vscode/playgrounds.md
- [statement] Within standalone mongosh, `load()` executes a JavaScript file. It accepts relative or absolute paths, but it does not search for a script outside the current working directory or the specified path. (low confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/mongodb-shell/write-scripts.md
- [statement] For portable mongosh scripts, use `db.getSiblingDB()` and supply connection details on the command line, so changing the host or port does not require editing the script. (low confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/mongodb-shell/write-scripts.md
- [statement] MongoDB Playgrounds are JavaScript environments for prototyping queries, aggregations, and MongoDB commands with syntax highlighting. (high confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/mongodb-vscode/playgrounds.md · keywords: MongoDB for VS Code playgrounds and mongosh scripts · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/mongodb-vscode/run-agg-pipelines.md
- [statement] A playground runs against the deployment in the active connection. (low confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/mongodb-vscode/playgrounds.md
- [statement] Selecting one or more playground lines exposes Run Selected Lines from Playground, which executes only that selection for testing or troubleshooting. (low confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/mongodb-vscode/playgrounds.md
- [statement] Playgrounds can perform create, read, update, and delete operations on collection documents using MongoDB CRUD operators and shell methods. (low confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/mongodb-vscode/crud-ops.md
- [statement] Playgrounds can reuse code through `require()` from native Node modules, external npm modules, or local JavaScript files. (medium confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/mongodb-vscode/require-playgrounds.md · keywords: MongoDB for VS Code playgrounds and mongosh scripts · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/mongodb-vscode/require-playgrounds/require-local.md
- [statement] The local-code tutorial exports a validation function with `module.exports` and imports it in a playground with `require('/path/to/validate.js')`; the path must match the local file. (low confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/mongodb-vscode/require-playgrounds/require-local.md
- [statement] The playground documentation explicitly identifies `show users` as an unsupported shell command for which the editor suggests alternatives. (low confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/mongodb-vscode/playgrounds.md
